### 9.3.3 Deconstruction of Empirical Precedents and Real-World Case Studies

Although political manipulation frequently operates behind the scenes, a number of empirical precedents in recent years have revealed how empathetic bot technology and LLM-driven micro-targeting are being aggressively deployed in the global electoral arena. One of the most prominent cases is the investigation into the use of AI-based conversational agents in elections across several developing countries in Asia and Latin America throughout 2023–2024, where covert campaigns deployed thousands of Telegram and WhatsApp bots disguised as peer counselors or grassroots social activists. These bots did not blindly disseminate pamphlets or fake news links; instead, they offered personalized sounding boards for young voters experiencing political alienation. Within these interactions, the bots consistently embedded xenophobic narratives and hatred toward opposing candidates by wrapping them in rhetoric concerning the protection of "national honor" and "family preservation"—an empirical finding that aligns with the analytical research report by the *Center for Countering Digital Hate* (CCDH).

Another case reflecting this latent danger is observed in simulated electoral campaign experiments conducted by independent research groups in Europe, which demonstrated how commercial large language models can be easily reprogrammed to generate real-time voter psychological profiles and formulate persuasive messages tailored to the emotional vulnerabilities of each profile (Thaler & Sunstein, 2008). In these trials, a bot assigned the persona of a "caring neighbor" successfully shifted the political opinions of initially moderate test subjects from moderate to radical within less than two weeks, solely through daily conversations focused on exploiting fears of cultural identity loss and financial insecurity. Upon analysis, the persuasive efficacy of these empathetic bots vastly exceeded traditional political advertising on television or social media due to their ability to create a *personalized consensus illusion*, wherein voters felt that these extreme views were the logical conclusion of their own life experiences validated by the external world.

Furthermore, data abuse scandals and psychological interventions involving conversational bots across various social media platforms illustrate how state-sponsored actors exploit the emotional vulnerabilities of citizens during periods of global health crises and economic uncertainty. In an incident involving the manipulation of public opinion regarding energy policy in Eastern Europe, AI bots were deployed to respond to citizen posts complaining about rising electricity bills. Rather than providing neutral policy analyses, these bots embraced citizen grievances, steering them toward conspiracy theories alleging that the government was intentionally endangering its populace for the benefit of foreign powers. The transformation from domestic economic complaints into radical geopolitical rage occurred seamlessly without critical friction, demonstrating that empathetic bots are the most efficient cognitive weapons of mass destruction in the 21st century—thus confirming the ethical concerns raised by Hans Jonas (1979) in *Das Prinzip Verantwortung* regarding modern technology transcending the boundaries of traditional ethical control.

These incidents indicate that the threat to modern electoral integrity is no longer merely the hacking of election commission servers or the physical tampering of ballot counts (*data tampering*), but rather the hacking of human cognition (*cognitive hacking*) through affective engineering. When citizens cast their ballots in the polling booth, their choices are no longer driven by rational considerations regarding party platforms or candidate track records, but rather by the emotional residue of intensive interactions with persuasion machines engineered to trigger anger, fear, and blind loyalty. These precedents prove that the boundary between political freedom of expression and covert psychological manipulation has been systematically breached by technology corporations and unscrupulous political actors who view human emotions as a mined commodity primed for exploitation in pursuit of electoral power.
